extracted.intended_audience: employers, HR professionals, labor attorneys, state/federal wage-and-hour enforcers, and other stakeholders affected by FLSA overtime exemption rules
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory standards governing how the Department of Labor will set and triennially update the part 541 EAP (executive, administrative, professional) salary and HCE thresholds, including notice, data, pause procedures, and the percentile methodologies selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triennial updates of standard salary and HCE thresholds (§541.607)
rubrics_metrics.description: New §541.607 establishes triennial updates of the standard salary level and the HCE total annual compensation threshold using the same methodologies used to set those thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes Department has not engaged in intervening rulemaking; the mechanism anticipates periodic updates every 3 years (first update, then a second update 3 years after the initial update). The Department intends these routine triennial updates to remain in force even if other methodology revisions are stayed or do not take effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use original-setting methodology for updates (not indexing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will update the earnings thresholds by applying the same methodology used to originally set the levels instead of indexing them for inflation (fixed percentile approach).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: fixed percentile approach eliminates risk that future levels deviate from the underlying salary-setting methodology; Department considered indexing (e.g., CPI-U) in prior rulemakings but chose fixed-percentile updates to preserve the screening function tied to a percentile of full-time salaried earnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-update resetting rule (expected percentiles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Absent further rulemaking, the Department anticipates the second update will reset the standard salary level to the 35th percentile of weekly earnings of full-time workers in the lowest-wage Census Region and reset the HCE threshold to the annualized weekly earnings of the 85th percentile of full-time salaried workers nationally based on contemporaneous data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reflects the Department's application of the final-rule methodologies for subsequent updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing: 150-day Federal Register notice and website posting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will publish in the Federal Register a notice with the adjusted standard salary level and HCE total annual compensation threshold not fewer than 150 days before the date the adjusted thresholds are set to take effect and will publish the updated thresholds on WHD's website no later than their effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters requested longer notice (e.g., 180 days to 1 year); Department concluded 150 days provides sufficient time for employers, particularly because the underlying BLS data set is publicly accessible and employers can anticipate adjustments before the Department's notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data window for updates: most recent 4 quarters of BLS data
rubrics_metrics.description: Updates will be based on the most recent available 4 quarters of data as published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics preceding the publication of the Department's notice with the adjusted levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters suggested alternatives (e.g., most recent 1 quarter, 6 quarters, or dropping recent quarters to account for employer preemptive actions); Department selected 4 quarters as balancing reflection of prevailing economic conditions with commenters' concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pause (delay) mechanism for scheduled updates
rubrics_metrics.description: A scheduled update may be paused while the Department engages in notice-and-comment rulemaking to change the earnings requirements and/or updating mechanism: if the Department publishes an NPRM proposing to change the salary methodology and/or modify the updating mechanism by the date it publishes the notice with adjusted thresholds, the scheduled update must be paused for 120 days beginning on the day the update was set to occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pause is triggered by publication of an NPRM proposing changes by the notice date; the pause will be lifted on the 121st day unless the Department finalizes a rule changing the methodology or updating mechanism by that time. The pause provides additional flexibility but does not limit the Department's normal rulemaking authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and timeframe of rulemaking flexibility (270-day window)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department retains the ability to engage in rulemaking at any time; the pause mechanism provides an additional 270-day context (150 days before the scheduled update plus 120 days after) in which the Department can complete rulemaking to alter a scheduled update.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters erroneously assumed the pause was the only means to change an update; Department clarifies it can engage in rulemaking outside the pause period as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigger standard for invoking pause: 'unforeseen economic or other conditions'
rubrics_metrics.description: §541.607(b)(4) is revised to permit triggering the pause where 'unforeseen economic or other conditions' warrant by issuing an NPRM proposing the changes by the date the Department publishes the notice with the adjusted thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department declines to further define 'unforeseen economic or other conditions' to preserve flexibility (COVID pandemic cited as an example). Lack of a narrow definition is intentional to avoid unduly limiting the Department's ability to respond to truly unanticipated circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of pause on next scheduled triennial update
rubrics_metrics.description: A pause on a scheduled update (120 days) will not affect the date for the next scheduled triennial update; the next update will occur 3 years from the date on which the delayed update would originally have been effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach maintains the regular updating schedule despite short delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability of triennial updates from methodology revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department intends for the triennial updates of the standard salary level and HCE threshold to be severable from revisions to the methodologies used to set those thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus, routine triennial updates under §541.607(b) will remain in force even if the methodologies established by the final rule are stayed or otherwise do not take effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard salary level methodology (final): 35th percentile, lowest-wage Census Region
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department is finalizing setting the standard salary level equal to the 35th percentile of earnings of full-time salaried workers in the lowest-wage Census Region (the South).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applying this methodology to 2023 data yields a salary level of $1,128 per week ($58,656 annually). Rationale: restores the salary level's screening function, accounts for the 2004 shift from a two-test to a one-test system, operates in combination with the standard duties test to better define bona fide EAP capacity, and lies between the long- and short-test salary levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: HCE total annual compensation threshold methodology (final): 85th percentile nationally
rubrics_metrics.description: The HCE total annual compensation threshold will be reset to the annualized weekly earnings of the 85th percentile of full-time salaried workers nationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective: ensure the HCE threshold serves as a streamlined alternative for those employees most likely to meet the standard duties test by excluding all but those employees 'at the very top of [the] economic ladder.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of salary tests historically: screening and enforcement function
rubrics_metrics.description: The salary test has historically been used as a screening tool and enforcement instrument to distinguish employees who are 'obviously nonexempt' and to simplify administration by providing a ready method of screening out obviously nonexempt employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department references the long-test methodology (traditionally set to exclude roughly the lowest-paid 10% in low-wage regions/industries) and the short-test role; these historical purposes inform the choice of percentile and the Department's desire to restore the salary test's screening function in a one-test regime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of BLS earnings data and percentiles to set thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will use BLS-published earnings data on full-time salaried workers and percentile calculations (e.g., 35th percentile for standard salary, 85th percentile for HCE) to set and update thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department's selected percentile methodologies build on past rulemakings (long/short tests and prior percentiles in 2004, 2016, 2019) and are applied to contemporaneous BLS data (most recent 4 quarters) for updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employers' ability to anticipate adjustments via public BLS data
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers will be able to access the BLS data set that will be used to make the adjustments and thus can anticipate the extent of the adjustment even before the Department publishes its notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fact is used to justify a 150-day notice period as sufficient for employer compliance planning; commenters' concerns about short notice were considered but rejected given data availability.
